claim_text: Our Safety First culture guided us through major expansion projects and helped us achieve our safety targets, ensuring our Great People go home safe and well every day.
metric_name: Australian operations TRIFR; Group TRIFR; Recordable injuries (Australia); Recordable injuries (Brazil)
context_text: Our Safety First culture guided us through major expansion projects and helped us achieve our safety targets, ensuring our Great People go home safe and well every day.；In FY25, we delivered a strong safety performance with both Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR) and Quality Safety Interactions Frequency Rate (QSIFR) targets achieved, and zero work-related fatalities recorded across all operations. At our Australian sites, comprising our Pilgangoora site, Projects and Perth office, we recorded a TRIFR of 2.79 with 14 recordable injuries, while our Group TRIFR was 3.10 including two recordable injuries in Brazil.
label: Suspected Greenwash
rationale_short: 虽然安全目标达成且零工亡，但报告期内仍有14起澳洲可记录伤害和2起巴西可记录伤害，与“go home safe and well every day”的绝对表述相矛盾。
notes: 同一句中既有可支持部分，也有被伤害数据直接否定的绝对表述。
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertion is that the company achieved its safety targets and that people go home safe and well every day. The provided evidence gives safety outcome metrics (Australian operations TRIFR 2.79; Group TRIFR 3.10; recordable injuries: Australia 14, Brazil 2), which substantively supports that safety performance was measured and that recordable injuries occurred at those levels. However, the evidence does not state what the “safety targets” were, whether they were achieved, or provide any comparison to a target/threshold or prior period. It also does not substantiate the absolute outcome “go home safe and well every day,” which is materially stronger than the evidence because the evidence reports recordable injuries.
